/-!
# Erdős Problem 248

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/248](https://www.erdosproblems.com/248)
- [TaTe25] T. Tao and J. Teräväinen, Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers. arXiv:2512.01739 (2025).
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.omega

namespace Erdos248

/--
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $\omega(n + k) \ll k$ for all $k \geq 1$?
Here $\omega(n)$ is the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos248.lean#L47"]
theorem erdos_248 : (∃ C > (0 : ℝ), { n | ∀ k ≥ 1, ω (n + k) ≤ C * k }.Infinite) := by
  sorry

end Erdos248

reformulations.difference: Lean allows n = 0 and uses a non-strict bound. Tao–Teräväinen explicitly use positive n, while Erdős’s original 1974 formulation uses a strict bound with an absolute constant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Removing the single possible witness n = 0 does not affect infinitude. A uniform bound ω(n+k) ≤ Ck implies ω(n+k) < (C+1)k for every k ≥ 1; a strict bound implies the non-strict bound with the same constant. The combined equivalence with an infinite set of positive n satisfying a strict bound was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as positive_strict_source_iff, without using the sorry-backed problem theorem.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the original problem. The absolute constant is uniform in both n and k, ω counts distinct prime divisors, and k ≥ 1 prevents evaluation at zero. Boundary computations and equivalence proofs compiled successfully. The affirmative statement and research-solved tag agree with Tao–Teräväinen’s Theorem 1.1, which proves the stronger Ω bound. The Erdős webpage was blocked by Cloudflare, so the original 1974 source and the cited paper were used. The linked formal theorem has the same statement; its downloaded dependency closure and compatibility patches showed no proof holes or additional axioms, but the external project was not independently rebuilt.
